title: Asa, King of Judah
lead: Asa ruled Judah for forty-one years (about 911–870 BC). Kings praises him as a reformer whose heart was whole with the LORD; Chronicles tells a fuller and darker story, of early faith rewarded and a late reliance on Aram and on doctors instead of God.

sections.b: Kings gives Asa sixteen verses: he removed the shrine men and idols, deposed the queen mother Maacah (his grandmother, on the usual reading), left the high places, and paid Ben-hadad of Damascus to break his treaty with Baasha (1 Kings 15:9–24). Chronicles gives him three chapters: reforms and ten quiet years, a great victory over Zerah the Cushite, a covenant to seek the LORD after Azariah's sermon, then the treaty with Aram condemned by Hanani the seer, the prophet in the stocks, and a final illness in which he sought healers, not the LORD (2 Chronicles 14–16).
